result.reason: The Company’s 30-day written-notice right and refund of prepaid post-termination fees substantially match the preferred position. However, Contractor may give notice while no SOW is outstanding even if the 90-day notice period later overlaps a new SOW, so the operative language does not reliably prevent Contractor from terminating during a committed engagement. The statement that Company has “no further liability” except for Services performed is also broader than necessary and could eliminate unrelated accrued obligations or agreed expenses. Adding termination of any SOW “in whole or in part” likewise goes beyond the original Agreement-level right and introduces avoidable scope and ambiguity. The margin comment does not cure these operative-language issues.
